13:12 Local Time, 11:12 GMT, 16:42 IST: A much better effort with the ball from Namibia, but they've still conceded a pile of runs. If Jordan Hermann scored a maiden ODI hundred the other day, today it was Connor Esterhuizen's turn. He was well supported by Tony de Zorzi and the pair added 183 runs for the second wicket. This partnership was followed by a few cameos, allowing the visitors to cruise past the 300-run mark. Namibia did come back well in the last few overs, but the damage had been done by then. Four wickets for the young Jack Brassell while Ruben Trumpelmann and Jan Balt took two each. Can Namibia chase down 335 and keep the series alive? Back shortly for the chase..

16:57 Local Time, 14:57 GMT, 20:27 IST: South Africa have stamped their authority on this game. It turned out to be another lopsided affair. Erasmus won the toss and once again chose to bowl. Their new-ball bowlers started well but the hosts lost their way through the middle overs. Esterhuizen's maiden ODI ton and de Zorzi's 79 set the platform for the visitors while a few breezy cameos from their lower middle-order enabled them to post 335 on the board. In reply, the duo of Duan Jansen and Eathan Bosch breathed fire with the new ball, thereby breaking the backbone of the hosts as they were reduced to 32/5. Erasmus batted well and struck a fifty but there was no real support from the other end. A couple of cameos from the tail just delayed the inevitable. Jansen took a 4-fer while Bosch finished things off with a 3-fer. Stick around for the presentations...
